unit.why: A brief anecdote: a tzaddik's son praises his father's devekut before the rebbe (R. Zvi), who answers with a witty teaching on divine names in every breath. It is a minimal narrative with an event and a reply.

stories.start_quote: עוד שם פ' ויצא וז"ל וכאשר
stories.end_quote: בשם הוי׳ ב"ה וב"ש עכדפח"ח עכ״ל
stories.summary_en: A tzaddik's son boasts that his father never broke his cleaving to God for twenty hours a day. The rebbe retorts that the father cleaved in every breath, drawing the breath in with the name Elohim and out with the Tetragrammaton.

tags.why: The anecdote centers on uninterrupted cleaving to God.

quotes: שבכל נשימה ונשימה כאשר המשיך אותה אל תוך הגוף
tags.why: It describes devekut sustained in every breath.

quotes: שבח בן צדיק אחד לפניו את אביו
tags.why: A tzaddik's son speaks about his father.

quotes: והשיב בצחות לשונו מה אתה אומר נער
tags.why: The rebbe's reply is a witty retort.

quotes: הי' בשם אלקים ובהתפשטות לחוץ הי' בשם הוי׳
tags.why: Contemplating divine names with each breath is a form of mystical concentration.
The point of the anecdote is a kabbalistic teaching quoted from a homiletic work.
It praises a tzaddik's spiritual virtue.
